_comment: WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets
work THROUGH. `make verify` and the CI `delegated-core-check` step both
read its green as 'the three delegated drivers still carry one lifecycle',
and nothing downstream re-derives that fact. A blind version of this check
would report exactly the same clean line while a driver's rendered region
quietly diverged - which is the pre-#1011 state, where three hand-kept
copies drifted ~60 lines apart and nobody was told.
THE CASES ARE WHOLE FIXTURE TREES, not the real repository. The gate takes
--root, so a case is a miniature repo: a tiny core template, three values
files, three driver documents. Deliberately small - the question is whether
the gate can tell a matching rendered region from a drifted one, not
whether it can render 540 lines. The fixture also exercises the
empty-block-slot path (codex and qwen leave STEP_EXTRA empty, gemma does
not), because 'the placeholder line disappears' is the rendering rule most
Stdlib-only and git-free, like the gate: no binary this fixture needs is
absent from the slim CI image, so the control gives the same verdict there

cases.name: bad-drifted
cases.why: One line of qwen's rendered region B edited in place, markers intact - the exact shape of someone fixing a lifecycle bug in a driver file instead of in the core. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see drift at all, which is the only thing it exists to see.

cases.name: good-matching
cases.why: The same tree with every region rendered from the core. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': a check that refuses every tree is indistinguishable from a working one on the bad case alone, and would block every merge until someone disabled it.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: this gate is new, so there is no previous blind version to vendor and the honest 'before' is 'no check at all', which cannot be run against a case. This is the plausible weaker check someone would write instead - confirm the marker pair is present and call that vendored. It catches deleted markers, and is blind to the failure that actually happens: a region edited in place with its markers intact. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
